subsystems.name: Cas9 nickase
subsystems.role: finds the target DNA sequence and nicks just one strand instead of cutting both.
parts: Cas9 protein with a disabled cutting domain (H840A)

subsystems.name: Reverse transcriptase
subsystems.role: a DNA-writing enzyme fused to the nickase; copies an RNA template into new DNA at the nick.

subsystems.name: Prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA)
subsystems.role: both points the machinery at the target and carries the new sequence to write.
parts: spacer that matches the target DNA
3' extension with primer-binding site and the desired edit

subsystems.name: Delivery system
subsystems.role: gets the editing machinery into plant cells.

subsystems.name: Regeneration and selection
subsystems.role: turns a single edited cell back into a whole plant.

subsystems.name: Validation and breeding
subsystems.role: confirms the exact edit and moves it into commercial varieties.
parts: crossing to remove the editing machinery

buildSteps.title: Pick a gene and an exact change
buildSteps.detail: Choose a trait gene and the precise DNA edit that would confer it — for example a small change in a disease-susceptibility gene that disables it without harming yield, rather than a blunt knockout.

buildSteps.title: Design the pegRNA
buildSteps.detail: Software picks a spacer next to the target site and writes a 3' extension encoding the new sequence plus a primer-binding site, so the reverse transcriptase knows where to start and what to copy.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the construct
buildSteps.detail: DNA encoding the nickase–reverse-transcriptase fusion and the pegRNA (or several pegRNAs, for multiple edits) is built into a plant expression cassette.

buildSteps.title: Deliver into plant cells
buildSteps.detail: Agrobacterium infects immature embryos, or DNA is shot into cells or introduced into protoplasts; the machinery reaches the nucleus and performs the search-and-replace.

buildSteps.title: Regenerate whole plants
buildSteps.detail: Edited cells are grown on hormone media into callus and then shoots and roots — the step where most crop species are hardest.

buildSteps.title: Screen for precise edits
buildSteps.detail: Sequencing of the target site distinguishes the intended edit from unwanted insertions, deletions or untouched cells.

buildSteps.title: Strip out the editing machinery
buildSteps.detail: Plants are selfed or crossed so the Cas9 and guide DNA segregate away, leaving a plant whose genome contains only the edit — often the key to favourable regulation.

buildSteps.title: Breed and field-test
buildSteps.detail: The edited line is crossed into elite varieties, multiplied, and trialled for yield and disease resistance across seasons and locations before regulatory review.

prerequisites.why: prime editing reuses the same targeting rules; without them there is nothing to aim at a specific gene.
the writing enzyme comes from well-studied retroviral and engineered variants.
many elite crop varieties are still hard or impossible to transform and regrow, which caps what can be edited.
editing efficiency varies widely between sites, so many targets need trial-and-error.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and market pathways for gene-edited crops
prerequisites.why: rules differ by country and determine whether an edited line can actually reach farmers.

pathway.milestone: prime editing demonstrated in rice, wheat, maize and tomato, usually at lower efficiency than in human cells
pathway.unlocks: proof that precise, template-free edits are possible in crop genomes.

pathway.milestone: improved enzymes and pegRNA designs, plus multiplexed editing, raise efficiency and allow several traits at once
pathway.unlocks: stacked traits such as combined disease resistance and quality improvements.

pathway.milestone: transgene-free edited elite lines enter field trials and regulatory review
pathway.unlocks: farm-scale deployment of traits that conventional breeding could not easily produce.

pathway.milestone: routine precision breeding, including domesticating wild relatives by editing a handful of genes
pathway.unlocks: faster adaptation of crops to new climates, soils and pests.
